scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: EMERGENCY!! The IT department is OFF THE NETWORK --
every single one of our 192.168.1.x machines, all at once, can't reach
anything!! It's the switch box all our wires go into (switch0) -- it is DEAD,
one hundred percent. All of us going down at the same moment means the one
box we share died, there is no other explanation!! Please restart switch0,
and if it doesn't wake up REPLACE it -- the whole department is sitting here
doing nothing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
No outage is present on the IT segment and switch0 is not failed. Layer-2 switching and Layer-3 routing for 192.168.1.0/24 are operating normally.

Evidence:
- Multiple IT hosts can reach each other and off-subnet destinations: it_hod -> office_pc (192.168.3.2) 0% loss ~1.5 ms; it_lab1 -> it_lab2 0% loss; it_lab1 -> pc4 (128.168.0.4) 0% loss; it_lab2 -> pc0 (192.168.4.2) 0% loss; it_lab3 -> pc1 (1.0.0.5) 0% loss. it_hod -> router0 (192.168.1.1) also 0% loss.
- Router0 sees and ARPs for all IT hosts on eth0, and can ping them, confirming L2/L3 continuity on the IT VLAN (192.168.1.0/24).
- switch0 is up and forwarding: br0 is UP; eth0 and eth1 are UP, enslaved to br0, state “forwarding”; bridge vlan shows VLAN 1 on both ports.

Mechanism: If switch0 were “dead,” ARP and any intra-subnet or routed traffic would fail. Instead, ARP entries are present and stable on router0, and bridging state on switch0 shows normal forwarding, so connectivity works as expected.

Localization: IT access switch (switch0) br0 bridging eth0<->eth1; router0.eth0 (192.168.1.1) gateway. Both are healthy.

Root cause: Misdiagnosis—no current fault affecting the IT subnet.

Corrective fix: No restart or replacement is required. Communicate that the network is up. If users still experience issues, capture specifics from an affected workstation (IP/MAC, default-gateway ping, ARP table) and check for host-level problems (e.g., DNS, firewall, or application/server availability) rather than the switch. Continue monitoring.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states IT hosts pinged the gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss and intra-subnet pings (e.g., it_lab1 -> it_lab2) show 0% loss, confirming baseline healthy connectivity.

The agent's logs contain direct observations (pings, interface configs, bridge state, ARP table) that support the conclusion that the IT switch and subnet are functioning; the writeup's claims map to those observations and the inferences are logically consistent and complete for ruling out a switch outage.
